literal_meaning: নিজের হাতে জগন্নাথ (one's own hand Jagannath)
figurative_meaning_en: An extremely miserly or stingy person
example_sentences_in_bangla: সে আপনা হাত জগন্নাথ, কখনো কাউকে অতিরিক্ত কিছু দেয় না।
এই লোকটি আপনা হাত জগন্নাথ বলে পরিচিত, সবসময় খরচে কৃপণতা করে।
example_sentences_in_english: He is a real 'Apna haat Jagannath', never gives anything extra to anyone.
This man is known as 'Apna haat Jagannath' for his constant miserliness in spending.
history: The idiom originates from the wooden idol of Lord Jagannath at the Puri temple in Odisha, which has stumps instead of proper hands, symbolizing minimalism or inability to hold or give generously, hence used for extremely stingy people.
note: The idiom draws from Hindu temple traditions and is widely used in Bengali folklore to critique avarice.
